descriptionChirho: A supernatural living being in the heavenly throne room, particularly the four living creatures of Revelation (cf. Ezekiel's cherubim). Translated as 'living creature(s)' (eng), 'ser(es) viviente(s)' (spa), 'viumbe-hai / kiumbe-hai' (swa), 'praanii' (hin), 'ka'inaat hayyah' (arb: living entities), 'saengmul' (kor: living being). Singular and plural forms represent the same referent type and merge into one sense.

An ordinary earthly animal or beast, as opposed to the celestial living creatures of the Apocalypse. Clearly distinguished across languages: 'animals' (eng), 'animales' (spa), 'wanyama' (swa: wild animals), 'pashuon' (hin: livestock/beasts), 'hayawanaat' (arb: animals), and 'jimseung' (kor: beast/livestock). This sense denotes natural fauna rather than heavenly beings, appearing in contexts like 2 Peter 2:12 and Jude 10.
